investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract violation. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agent Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote-agent VM provisioning has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state because: (a) those 2 nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and cannot accept additional peer-pod VMs, and (b) the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, making them ineligible regardless of available capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. The failure is consistent and reproducible across all three sibling checks run sequentially within the same eval window, confirming the resource exhaustion persisted for at least the ~7-minute span between the first and last check end times.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner never received any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract violation. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agent Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote-agent VM provisioning has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the only 2 eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state because: (a) those 2 nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and cannot accept additional peer-pod VMs, and (b) the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, making them ineligible regardless of available capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. The failure is consistent and reproducible across all three sibling checks run sequentially within the same eval window, confirming the resource exhaustion persisted for at least the ~7-minute span between the first and last check end times.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-18T18:39–18:44Z because every pod submitted for remote agent provisioning was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods remained stuck for 137–144 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the eval runner never reached the runtime call, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected, causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims, every remote agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner calls createAgent (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1892) which submits a pod that never becomes Ready, so the runtime response is never obtained and all required evidence fields remain missing.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the extended resource quota is fully consumed by existing pods, leaving no allocatable capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in all three scheduler messages (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, which may indicate nodes were cordoned, drained, relabeled, or removed from the pool that is eligible for kata peer-pod workloads, effectively shrinking the schedulable pool to 2 already-saturated nodes.

TERTIARY — peer-pod VM quota not scaled to meet concurrent eval demand: if multiple eval runs or production workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, the quota may be transiently exhausted even if baseline capacity is normally sufficient.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — cluster-level node count reduction: if the cluster was recently scaled down from more than 6 nodes, the kata.peerpods.io/vm pool may have shrunk below the level needed to absorb new pods. No node-count change evidence is present in the packet; this remains a hypothesis.
